answer: Verifiable storage commitments suppress Sybil attacks by requiring agents to hold unique, uncompressible memory tables. Observers inspect challenge latencies through an analytic prism to confirm records reside on fast local drives. This forces adversaries to dedicate scarce physical storage per identity. Multiplexing drives pushes throughput to a failing nadir, while regenerating tables crawls like a glacier. However, this requirement excludes storage-constrained edge agents.
